core_obligations: Use that f is local complete intersection, record f^![Y] = [X], and express alpha and beta through the Chern character and the fundamental classes (proof lines 13928-13940).
Run the chain of equalities using commutation of f^! with bivariant classes, centrality of Chern classes and bivariance for the pushforward (proof lines 13942-13960).
proof_roadmap: The local complete intersection property and the K-theoretic description of the classes (proof lines 13928-13940).
The chain of equalities and conclusion (proof lines 13942-13960).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for f : X -> Y a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over (S, delta) with both X and Y quasi-compact, regular, of affine diagonal and finite dimension, f is a local complete intersection morphism, and that if moreover the Gysin map exists for f and f is proper then f_*(alpha . f^!beta) = f_*alpha . beta in CH^*(Y) otimes Q for the intersection product of the regular section (statement lines 13912-13926). The first assertion is More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-morphism-regular-schemes-is-lci; the proof notes f^![Y] = [X] by Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-easy, writes alpha = ch(alpha') cap [X] and beta = ch(beta') cap [Y] with alpha', beta' in K_0(Vect) otimes Q as in the construction of that intersection product, and sets c = ch(alpha'), c' = ch(beta') (proof lines 13928-13940). The conclusion is then a six term chain: replace beta by its description, move f^! past the bivariant class c' using Lemma labelled lemma-lci-gysin-commutes, substitute f^![Y] = [X], reorder the two cappings using that Chern classes are central in the bivariant ring, commute c' with f_* by bivariance, and read the result back as beta . f_*alpha (proof lines 13942-13960). Recognising that the regularly embedded situation admits the same bivariant bookkeeping as the smooth case, with the Chern character providing the bridge to K-theory, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
